This relative volume of transactions becomes important when you consider that,
according to the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, the best estimate for the amount of
all global criminal proceeds available for laundering through the financial system in 2009 was
$1.6 trillion.

statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires financial institutions to report transactions that are suspicious, such as those involving illegal activity or lacking a business purpose. In this case, the individual's transactions are consistent with their KYC profile as a self-employed proprietor with an expected monthly volume of $33,146. The transaction amounts (ranging from approximately $861 to $3,497) and the variety of counterparties (LLCs and individuals) align with normal small-business cash flow. Because there is no evidence of structuring, money laundering, or anomalies relative to the profile, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires reporting of suspicious activity but no such triggers are present here.
